title: WPSB/134/2013 of Vibhava Prakash Mishra Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/B) No. 134 of 2013
Vibhava Prakash Mishra. .......... Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others. .......... Respondents
Mr. Arvind Vashisht, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. K.P. Upadhyaya, Chief Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand /
respondent Nos. 1 & 3.
Mr. B.D. Kandpal, Advocate for respondent No. 2.

JUDGMENT
Coram: Hon'ble Barin Ghosh, C.J.
 Hon'ble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.

BARIN GHOSH, C. J. (Oral)
 We are not inclined to entertain the writ petition. Petitioner
contends that the advertisement, though mentioned a specific number of
vacancies, it also provided that the number may increase or decrease. It
has been stated that, under the Rules, a wait list is required to be prepared
and the petitioner is in the wait list. It has been stated that
recommendations for the advertised vacancies have been made, but, while
doing so, recommendations for the vacancies, which cropped-up during
the recruitment years 2009-2010 and 2010-2011, have not been made. It
is stated that, in the event recommendations for those vacancies are also
made, petitioner will be recommended.
2. No sooner recommendations were made for the posts already
advertised, unless it is shown and established that any recommendee,
thereafter, has refused to join the post on being appointed on the basis of
such recommendation, the wait list lapsed. The recommendations could
not be acted upon in view of interim order that was passed by this Court.
That interim order has been vacated yesterday. As a result, those
recommendations can only be acted upon from now onwards. It is too
early for the petitioner to contend, therefore, that the wait list is still alive.
He would be in a position to contend that the wait list is alive only when a

2
person, appointed pursuant to the recommendation, refuses to join. For
the time being, petitioner must proceed on the basis that, since all the
advertised posts have been recommended, the wait list stands lapsed.
3. The other contention is that four posts, available for differently
abled people, have not been supplied because of want and, accordingly,
since they are horizontal reservations, be supplied. The fact remains that
those differently abled people occupy specified points in the 100 point
roster. They are not, as such, horizontal reservations.
4. The writ petition, accordingly, fails and the same is dismissed.

(Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.) (Barin Ghosh, C. J.)
 01.05.2013 01.05.2013
G
